Ukrainian drone manufacturer SkyFall has shown Associated Press its new StarGate aerial medical evacuation drone, developed at the request of the 475th Assault Regiment (Code 9.2).
The drone can carry 150 kg, fly up to 15 km and reach speeds of 105 km/h. It has already been delivered to Ukrainian troops for frontline testing.
Evacuating wounded soldiers by air using drones is still a largely untested concept. Any technical failure during flight could be fatal, especially over a battlefield saturated with attack drones.
However, StarGate is designed for extreme situations where ground evacuation is impossible or every minute counts.
It’s essentially a matter of risk management: sometimes a dangerous flight may be the only chance to save a critically wounded soldier who would otherwise be left behind.

items.title: Ukraine’s SkyFall has developed StarGate, a heavy CASEVAC drone designed to evacuate wounded troops from frontline kill zones under fire and across minefields. The six-rotor drone can carry up to 150 kg, fly 15 km one way and reach 105 km/h. It uses Starlink and SkyFall’s L-Link, while integrated AI allows navigation without GPS and can return the aircraft to safety if communications are completely lost. Frontline testing began with a Ukrainian combat brigade in October. #Ukraine

"Ukrainian troops have been caught off guard by restrictions on Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite internet systems that disrupted frontline operations, while Kyiv received no advance warning from its partners of a Russian missile attack on its energy facilities for the second day running, according to Ukrainian officials.

Russia is targeting yet another power plant and the lives of our people.

It is important that the world does not stay silent about this. And it is important that the United States really see what is happening and who is responsible for this war continuing.

After Ukrainian drones hit Yandex data centers, a viral chart showed Russian "bot traffic" collapsing. But those bots are mostly Yandex's own search crawlers, not the info-ops social media accounts.
